must_remember: Classical free electron theory treats valence electrons using Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics, while the quantum model uses Fermi-Dirac statistics.
The Fermi energy ($E_F$) is the maximum energy level occupied by electrons at absolute zero ($T = 0$ K).
Only a small fraction of electrons near the Fermi surface participate in thermal excitation, resolving the specific heat paradox.
The Wiedemann-Franz law relates thermal conductivity ($\kappa$) and electrical conductivity ($\sigma$) through the Lorenz number $L$.
Drift velocity ($v_d = \mu E$) is extremely small, typically on the order of millimeters per second, despite high Fermi velocities.

glossary.meaning: The maximum energy state occupied by electrons in a metal at absolute zero temperature.
The average time between successive collisions of an electron with ion cores in a metal.
The number of allowed quantum states per unit volume per unit energy interval.
A law stating that the ratio of thermal conductivity to electrical conductivity is directly proportional to temperature.
